newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh and Burma exchange prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh and Burma exchange prisoners.

text.p: Bangladesh and Burma exchanged 36 prisoners at a meeting on Saturday between their border forces, Bangladeshi officials said.
They said Bangladesh handed over 27 Burmese nationals arrested recently for infiltrating into this country and in return brought home nine fishermen seized by Burma's Nasaka border guards last month.
The meeting took place on Saturday at Maungdow township in West Burma's Arakan state, bordering Bangladesh's Cox's Bazar district.
"We had frindly discussions...including repatriation of Burmese refugees and strengthening cooperation along our borders," one official told reporters. He did not give details.
Six Bangladeshis and two wild elephants were killed early last month by land mines at Naikhyangchhari, along the frontier.
Police said the mines had been planted by Burmese troops trying to prevent cross-border insurgency.
More than 250,000 Moslems, called Rohingyas, fled to southeastern Bangladesh in early 1992 from the Moslem-majority Arakan, complaining of military persecution.
Repatriation began in September that year following an agreement between Dhaka and Rangoon, but some 50,000 are still left squalid camps, according to official figures.
